entries.title: Embedded Private Key Material
entries.description: The checked source contains a private-key block. Determine whether the key is active, a test fixture, or publicly distributed material.
entries.impact: An exposed active private key may allow impersonation, unauthorized signatures, or decryption where the corresponding protocol and key usage permit it.
entries.remediation: Remove active private keys from source and distributed artifacts. Revoke or rotate exposed keys, and store replacements in a restricted key-management service.

entries.title: Credentials in Connection URL
entries.description: A connection URL or authorization header embeds credential material directly in the checked source.
entries.impact: Anyone who can read the source, build artifacts, or copied configuration may recover active credentials and access the associated service with the credential owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation: Remove embedded credentials and load them from an approved secret store. Rotate exposed active credentials and restrict their privileges and lifetime.

entries.title: Unsigned JWT Algorithm Selection
entries.description: JWT configuration or processing explicitly selects an unsigned algorithm.
entries.impact: If unsigned tokens are accepted as authenticated claims, an attacker may forge identity, roles, or other trusted claims and gain unauthorized access.
entries.remediation: Require signature verification with a fixed allowlist of approved algorithms and trusted keys. Reject unsigned tokens and validate issuer, audience, and expiry.

entries.title: TLS Verification Disabled By Environment
entries.description: The checked code or configuration bypasses a certificate, hostname, or server-trust decision. Resolve the effective callback and build configuration before confirming a production bypass.
entries.impact: A network attacker may impersonate the intended server and read or modify traffic if the bypass accepts an untrusted certificate or mismatched hostname on a reachable connection.
entries.remediation: Restore platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Reject invalid server trust, remove permissive callbacks and environment overrides from production, and use properly configured test trust stores for development.

entries.title: Sensitive Data Logging Review

entries.description: Diagnostic output or execution tracing includes values that may contain credentials, tokens, or private user data.

entries.title: Cross-Origin Access Policy Review

entries.remediation: Allow only the exact trusted origins required by the feature. Authenticate and authorize each operation independently; validate message origin and content before invoking native functionality.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review

entries.title: WebView Debugging Policy Review

Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.impact: Sensitive keychain items may become accessible to other applications in the permitted group, expanding the credential trust boundary beyond a single application.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.title: Associated Domain Configuration Review
entries.description: The application registers or parses an externally supplied URI or link. Registration alone does not establish unsafe routing or authorization. Resolve the particular connection, host and client configuration selected by the shipped build.
entries.remediation: Allowlist accepted schemes, hosts, paths, and operations. Validate link parameters, require authorization before sensitive actions, and verify domain association when relying on trusted web links. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.
entries.impact: A crafted link may trigger unauthorized actions, redirect navigation, or expose private data if the receiving handler trusts URI fields or bypasses authentication and object-level authorization.
entries.reviewer: Test invalid chains, wrong hostnames, redirects and build-specific exceptions; an unrelated trusted client or HTTPS URL does not protect this connection. Missing pinning alone is not proof of insecurity.

entries.title: TLS Hostname Validation Review
entries.description: The checked code or configuration bypasses a certificate, hostname, or server-trust decision. Resolve the effective callback and build configuration before confirming a production bypass. Resolve the exact declaration or operation in the selected build and identify its security boundary.
entries.remediation: Restore platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Reject invalid server trust, remove permissive callbacks and environment overrides from production, and use properly configured test trust stores for development. Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.
entries.impact: A network attacker may impersonate the intended server and read or modify traffic if the bypass accepts an untrusted certificate or mismatched hostname on a reachable connection.
entries.reviewer: Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.

entries.title: Hardcoded Authentication Review
entries.description: Authentication-related code compares against a literal value. Determine whether it is a real credential check, a test fixture, or a non-secret state comparison. Trace the actual authorization decision, credential binding and failure path rather than accepting a local success marker.
entries.remediation: Remove embedded authentication secrets and enforce authentication through a trusted verifier. Rotate exposed active values and keep test-only bypasses out of release builds. Enforce authorization on the trusted server and bind local authentication to protected keys or credentials where required; use external-browser authorization and proof-key protection for public native clients.
entries.impact: If a distributed constant acts as an authentication secret or grants privileged access, someone who recovers it may impersonate a user or bypass the intended authentication process.
entries.reviewer: Test cancellation, device-credential fallback, enrollment changes, stale reuse windows, redirect interception and unavailable secure storage; local biometrics do not replace server authorization.

entries.title: Content Provider Query Review
entries.positive: override fun query(uri: Uri, projection: Array<String>?, selection: String?, args: Array<String>?, order: String?): Cursor? { return db.rawQuery(selection, args) }
entries.description: The application queries a content provider. Determine the provider’s trust, returned data sensitivity, and any selection built from external input. Resolve the external entry point, its caller or URI grant, and the sensitive operation or resource reached.
entries.remediation: Validate provider authority and permissions, bind selection arguments, and authorize each data operation. Limit requested columns and avoid logging sensitive results. Minimize exported surfaces and URI grants; validate parsed schemes, hosts and paths, use verified links where appropriate, and authorize each sensitive action.
entries.impact: Private provider data may be disclosed or modified if the provider lacks effective caller authorization or if attacker-controlled selection text changes the intended query.
entries.reviewer: Resolve merged manifests, aliases and SDK defaults; test custom-scheme collision, malformed URLs, encoded paths, nested intents, read/write grants and permission inheritance. Registration or permission presence alone does not prove unauthorized access.

entries.title: WebView File Access Review
entries.description: A file provider, plugin, or WebView permits access to a broad filesystem scope or relaxes file-origin isolation. Resolve the loaded content and frame origin, the exact WebView instance, and the native operations available to that content.
entries.remediation: Expose only dedicated app-owned sharing directories. Keep WebView file-origin and universal access disabled where possible, validate navigation, and issue narrowly scoped temporary file grants only to intended recipients. Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.
entries.impact: Untrusted content or a recipient with a usable file grant may read private files, disclose stored credentials, or access resources outside the directory intended for sharing.
entries.reviewer: Test subframes, redirects, javascript/data/content URLs, deceptive host suffixes, and a safe WebView beside an unsafe instance; JavaScript enablement alone is not a vulnerability.

entries.title: WebView Debugging Policy Review
entries.description: WebView remote debugging or inspection is explicitly enabled. Determine whether the setting reaches a distributed production build. Resolve the loaded content and frame origin, the exact WebView instance, and the native operations available to that content.
entries.remediation: Enable WebView inspection only in verified development builds. Disable it in distributed releases and verify the setting in the final application artifact. Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.
entries.impact: A party with access to the platform’s debugging interface may inspect page content, extract session data, or execute scripts in the application’s WebView when production debugging remains accessible.
entries.reviewer: Test subframes, redirects, javascript/data/content URLs, deceptive host suffixes, and a safe WebView beside an unsafe instance; JavaScript enablement alone is not a vulnerability.

entries.title: SMS Reception Capability
entries.description: The application sends SMS messages or declares a capability to receive or inspect SMS content. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.remediation: Request only the SMS capabilities needed by a user-visible feature. Require explicit intent for sending, protect received message content, and prevent logs or unauthorized uploads of verification codes. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.impact: Unauthorized SMS handling may expose verification codes or private messages, cause unwanted messaging charges, or affect account recovery if the relevant permission and execution path are available.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: Package Management Capability
entries.description: The application requests or uses package installation or broad package-discovery capabilities. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.remediation: Use scoped package queries and platform installation prompts. Require clear user intent for installation, verify the package source and integrity, and avoid collecting an unnecessary application inventory. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.impact: Unapproved installation may introduce executable software, and broad package discovery may reveal sensitive information about the user’s installed applications when consent or data-use controls are inadequate.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: Cross-Application Overlay Capability
entries.description: The application requests permission to draw over other applications. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.remediation: Use overlays only for a transparent user-authorized feature. Avoid sensitive input capture, make overlays dismissible, and honor platform restrictions on protected screens. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.impact: An authorized overlay may obscure trusted interface elements or imitate prompts, enabling misleading interactions or credential capture if the feature is misused.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: Background Execution Capability
entries.description: The manifest declares background-service, boot, wake-lock, or related persistence capabilities. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.remediation: Limit background execution to justified tasks, provide required user-visible notifications and controls, and stop services and release wake locks when their work ends. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.impact: Unnecessary or undisclosed background activity may prolong data collection, consume device resources, or continue network activity beyond the user’s expected application lifecycle.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: Broad External Storage Capability
entries.description: The application declares or uses broadly accessible storage. Resolve the actual directories, access mode, platform version, and sensitivity of stored data. Identify the value written, backing store and access class, including backup, restore, reinstall and logout behavior.
entries.remediation: Keep private data in app-private storage and use platform-scoped access for deliberate sharing. Authenticate or validate externally read files and avoid storing executable or credential material in shared locations. Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.impact: Other actors with access to shared storage may read sensitive files or replace content later consumed by the application, compromising confidentiality or integrity.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.title: App Transport Security Review
entries.description: The effective transport policy may permit insecure HTTP content or relax transport protections for a WebView, media request, domain, or application. Resolve the exact declaration or operation in the selected build and identify its security boundary.
entries.remediation: Use HTTPS with normal certificate validation. Remove unnecessary transport exceptions, keep any unavoidable exception narrowly scoped, and avoid sending credentials or loading executable content over cleartext connections. Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.
entries.impact: A network attacker may read or modify affected cleartext traffic. Modified executable web content may also compromise the containing WebView session or exposed native interfaces.
entries.reviewer: Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.

entries.title: Debug Task Entitlement in Apple Configuration
entries.description: Apple application configuration enables the debug-task entitlement. Verify the entitlement in the signed distribution artifact. Resolve the exact declaration or operation in the selected build and identify its security boundary.
entries.remediation: Remove debug-task entitlements from distribution builds. Verify the final signed entitlement set and keep production authorization enforced independently of the client process. Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.
entries.impact: An actor with the necessary device access may attach a debugger to the distributed application and inspect or alter its process, potentially exposing in-memory secrets or bypassing client-side checks.
entries.reviewer: Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.

entries.title: Application File Sharing Review
entries.description: Application configuration makes its document directory available through file sharing or document browsing. Identify the value written, backing store and access class, including backup, restore, reinstall and logout behavior.
entries.remediation: Keep credentials and private internal files outside shared document directories. Disable unnecessary sharing or expose only documents deliberately approved for external access. Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.impact: Private files stored in the exposed directory may be read or copied outside the application’s intended access boundary by users or other applications with permitted document access.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.title: Android Runtime Method Hooking
entries.description: The code dynamically loads executable material or alters runtime method dispatch. Resolve the source, integrity checks, and intended use of that material. Resolve the exact declaration or operation in the selected build and identify its security boundary.
entries.remediation: Load only approved code from trusted locations, verify integrity and authenticity before loading, and keep runtime hooks confined to documented, authorized behavior. Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.
entries.impact: A party able to replace loaded code or control a runtime hook may execute with the application’s privileges, inspect private data, or alter security decisions. Legitimate bundled code and instrumentation do not establish an attack.
entries.reviewer: Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.

entries.title: Clipboard Read Capability
entries.description: The application reads the shared clipboard or pasteboard. Review whether the read follows an explicit paste action and whether the returned content enters logs, storage, or network requests. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.remediation: Read clipboard content only for an explicit user paste action. Process only the value needed for that action, avoid logging or transmitting it unnecessarily, and respect platform clipboard access restrictions. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.impact: Passwords, payment details, or other private content copied from another application could be collected or disclosed if clipboard reads occur without user intent or the content is sent to an unauthorized recipient. Platform access restrictions and the actual handling of the data determine exposure.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: Cryptographic Algorithm Use Review
entries.description: The checked cryptographic configuration uses a constant embedded key, ECB mode, or a legacy algorithm. Establish whether the operation protects confidential or integrity-sensitive data. Determine whether the operation protects secrets, authenticates data or serves a non-security purpose; resolve algorithm, mode and key provenance.
entries.remediation: Keep encryption keys in an appropriate key-management facility and use modern authenticated encryption for confidential data. Migrate legacy ciphertext safely, with unique nonces and keys appropriate to the selected algorithm. Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.
entries.impact: Embedded keys can be recovered from distributed code, and unsuitable algorithms or ECB mode may expose plaintext relationships or weaken confidentiality. Consequences depend on key handling, data format, and the security purpose of the operation.
entries.reviewer: Distinguish checksums from authentication, asymmetric RSA transformations from symmetric ECB, and test IV/nonce reuse, fixed keys and algorithm migration.

entries.title: Sensitive Input Masking Review
entries.description: A text field whose identifier indicates secret input explicitly disables secure entry. Confirm the field’s content and whether an intentional reveal action limits this behavior. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.impact: An observer or recording mechanism may capture displayed credentials or secrets while the field is unmasked. Identifier matching alone does not establish that the field contains a secret.
entries.remediation: Enable secure entry for secret input by default. If a reveal feature is necessary, require explicit user intent and restore masking when the screen loses focus. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: TLS Hostname Validation Review
entries.description: A stream SSL configuration explicitly disables the peer-name check. Verify the configuration is used by a reachable connection and inspect any independent hostname validation. Resolve the particular connection, host and client configuration selected by the shipped build.
entries.impact: A network attacker with a certificate valid for another name may impersonate the expected endpoint if certificate-to-hostname matching is disabled without an equivalent check.
entries.remediation: Retain certificate chain validation and match the peer name to the intended host. Remove null peer-name overrides from production connection settings. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.
entries.reviewer: Test invalid chains, wrong hostnames, redirects and build-specific exceptions; an unrelated trusted client or HTTPS URL does not protect this connection. Missing pinning alone is not proof of insecurity.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: A stream SSL configuration explicitly disables certificate-chain validation. Confirm the setting is applied to a network connection and whether equivalent trust validation exists. Resolve the particular connection, host and client configuration selected by the shipped build.
entries.impact: A network attacker may use an untrusted certificate to intercept or modify traffic when the disabled platform check is not replaced with effective validation.
entries.remediation: Use platform certificate-chain and hostname validation. Keep development trust exceptions isolated from distributed releases. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.
entries.reviewer: Test invalid chains, wrong hostnames, redirects and build-specific exceptions; an unrelated trusted client or HTTPS URL does not protect this connection. Missing pinning alone is not proof of insecurity.

entries.title: Biometric Key Invalidation Review
entries.description: A key policy explicitly disables invalidation after biometric enrollment changes. Verify biometric-only key authentication, credential fallback, key lifetime and applicable platform behavior. Trace the actual authorization decision, credential binding and failure path rather than accepting a local success marker.
entries.impact: A person able to enroll a new biometric may gain access to an existing protected key if the key’s effective policy accepts the new enrollment. This risk depends on authentication configuration.
entries.remediation: Invalidate biometric-bound keys when enrollment changes where the threat model requires it. Verify the effective key policy and use authenticated cryptographic operations for sensitive actions. Enforce authorization on the trusted server and bind local authentication to protected keys or credentials where required; use external-browser authorization and proof-key protection for public native clients.
entries.reviewer: Test cancellation, device-credential fallback, enrollment changes, stale reuse windows, redirect interception and unavailable secure storage; local biometrics do not replace server authorization.

entries.title: Screen Capture Protection Review
entries.description: An activity explicitly allows screenshots for the recent-task preview. Determine whether sensitive content is visible and whether other window protections prevent capture. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.impact: Sensitive content visible during background transitions may appear in the task switcher when the effective window policy permits a preview.
entries.remediation: Disable recent-task screenshots for sensitive activities and apply the appropriate secure-window policy. Verify background transitions and screen recording on supported devices. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: WebView Content Access Review
entries.description: WebView settings explicitly enable content-provider URL access. Identify loaded origins, provider permissions and whether untrusted content can request sensitive content URIs. Resolve the loaded content and frame origin, the exact WebView instance, and the native operations available to that content.
entries.impact: Untrusted content may access provider data reachable through the WebView when origin restrictions and provider controls are insufficient. Enabling this capability alone does not prove a data leak.
entries.remediation: Disable content access when unnecessary. Restrict loaded origins and provider access, and test content-URI reads from untrusted WebView pages. Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.
entries.reviewer: Test subframes, redirects, javascript/data/content URLs, deceptive host suffixes, and a safe WebView beside an unsafe instance; JavaScript enablement alone is not a vulnerability.

entries.title: Preferences Data Storage Review
entries.positive: SharedPreferences prefs = getSharedPreferences("user", MODE_PRIVATE); SharedPreferences.Editor editor = prefs.edit(); editor.putString("password", password);
entries.description: A preferences editor writes a value under a credential-related key. Resolve the actual backing store and whether the value is protected; MODE_PRIVATE restricts access but does not encrypt stored values. Identify the value written, backing store and access class, including backup, restore, reinstall and logout behavior.
entries.impact: If the stored value is a reusable unprotected credential, access to application files or permitted backups may expose it and allow unauthorized account use.
entries.remediation: Avoid retaining passwords. Use revocable session credentials with appropriate platform-backed protection, minimize retention and exclude secrets from backups. Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.title: Verification Code Written to Console
entries.description: Verification-code data is passed directly to a console logging call.
entries.impact: Captured logs may disclose usable verification codes while they remain valid.
entries.remediation: Remove verification-code values from logs; test release logging and retention.

entries.title: URL Query Encoding Review
entries.description: A direct request template interpolates a raw variable into an address or search query value.
entries.impact: Delimiter characters may change query parameters and request meaning; destination control and SSRF are not established.
entries.remediation: Encode each query value with URLSearchParams or encodeURIComponent; validate endpoint-specific requirements.

entries.title: Camera Response Validation Review
entries.description: An image-picker callback dereferences the first asset without a recognized local nonempty-assets guard.
entries.impact: An empty or error result may cause a local exception and disrupt the image operation.
entries.remediation: Handle cancellation and errors, require a nonempty assets array before indexing, and settle every operation outcome.

entries.title: State Persistence Review
entries.description: An unrestricted ordinary-storage persistence configuration occurs alongside an authentication reducer declaration. This is file-level configuration review, not a proved stored-secret flow.
entries.impact: Sensitive authentication state may persist without appropriate protection if this configuration actually includes those fields.
entries.remediation: Resolve the persisted reducer and fields; exclude sensitive state or use protected storage, and verify logout and account switching.

entries.title: Authentication Placeholder Token Review
entries.description: A recognized sign-in or token-setting call receives a literal placeholder token.
entries.impact: Shipped prototype logic may enter a local authenticated state without verified credentials; server access is not established.
entries.remediation: Replace placeholder session values with a verified authentication result; exclude test and demonstration code from release behavior.

entries.title: Upload Quota Enforcement Review
entries.description: A numeric limit checks only an incoming batch before a direct spread-based append to an existing collection.
entries.impact: Repeated additions may exceed the intended collection limit; receiving-service limits and actual resource impact remain unverified.
entries.remediation: Validate existing plus incoming count and decoded size; enforce applicable limits at the receiving service as well.

entries.title: Sensitive Data Logging Review
entries.description: A PHP logging message directly includes a secret-like variable. Confirm the value, effective logging configuration, access and retention.
entries.impact: If the value holds an active password, token or key, readable logs may disclose credentials and permit access with their privileges.
entries.remediation: Remove passwords, tokens and secret keys from log messages. Use non-sensitive identifiers and verify release log access and retention.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: A datasource bean contains a literal password. Short passwords remain relevant. Configuration presence does not establish that the credential is active or deployed.
entries.impact: Readers of deployed source or configuration may recover the database credential and gain access with its effective privileges.
entries.remediation: Load database passwords from a restricted secret store. Rotate exposed active credentials and restrict the database account.

entries.title: WebView Permission Policy Review
entries.description: A grant() call receives the entire resource list from the same request. Resolve whether this is a WebView PermissionRequest and whether the origin, requested resources and Android permissions are checked before granting access.
entries.impact: Untrusted frames or navigation may reach privileged native operations or expose session data if origin isolation and per-operation authorization are insufficient.
entries.remediation: Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.
entries.reviewer: Test subframes, redirects, javascript/data/content URLs, deceptive host suffixes, and a safe WebView beside an unsafe instance; JavaScript enablement alone is not a vulnerability.

entries.title: WebView Permission Policy Review
entries.description: A callback is invoked with the received origin and an affirmative permission result. Resolve whether it is a WebView geolocation callback and whether the user authorized this exact origin.
entries.impact: Untrusted frames or navigation may reach privileged native operations or expose session data if origin isolation and per-operation authorization are insufficient.
entries.remediation: Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.
entries.reviewer: Test subframes, redirects, javascript/data/content URLs, deceptive host suffixes, and a safe WebView beside an unsafe instance; JavaScript enablement alone is not a vulnerability.

entries.title: Fragment Validation Accepts Every Class
entries.positive: override fun isValidFragment(name: String): Boolean = true
entries.negative: override fun isValidFragment(name: String): Boolean = allowed.contains(name)
entries.description: The isValidFragment override unconditionally returns true. Determine whether an externally supplied fragment class can reach a privileged preference activity in the application's supported Android versions.
entries.impact: The observed behavior may weaken confidentiality, integrity or availability when exposed to an untrusted caller or sensitive value.
entries.remediation: Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.
entries.reviewer: Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.

entries.title: Archive Entry Controls Extraction Destination
entries.description: The code uses archive-entry or extraction APIs. Trace names supplied by each archive entry to the actual output file; the marker alone does not establish an unsafe write.
entries.impact: Untrusted content may execute privileged behavior or overwrite files if integrity, type constraints or destination containment are ineffective.
entries.remediation: Verify signed updates and compatibility, restrict decoded types, and enforce canonical destination containment before extraction or execution.
entries.reviewer: Test tampered updates, downgrade/replay, absolute paths, traversal, sibling-prefix and symlink escapes, size limits and partial failure; an unrelated validation call does not protect this operation.

entries.title: Backup Scope Review
entries.description: An active backup configuration includes a whole storage root. Resolve the particular cloud-backup or device-transfer section, its domain and effective exclude rules; an include declaration alone does not prove that sensitive data is backed up.
entries.impact: Recoverable sensitive values may expose sessions or private data to a party able to access the relevant storage, backup or shared device.
entries.remediation: Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.title: Network Credential Persistence Review
entries.positive: let credential = URLCredential(user: user, password: password, persistence: .permanent)
entries.negative: let credential = URLCredential(user: user, password: password, persistence: .forSession)
entries.description: Network credential creation selects permanent persistence. Identify the credential type, backing store, account scope and whether this lifetime is intended for the supplied secret.
entries.impact: Recoverable sensitive values may expose sessions or private data to a party able to access the relevant storage, backup or shared device.
entries.remediation: Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.title: Clipboard Data Exposure Review
entries.description: A variable named as sensitive is written to the general pasteboard. Confirm the actual value and whether cross-application or cross-device sharing and clipboard lifetime meet the application's policy.
entries.impact: Sensitive information may reach logs, other applications, keyboard services, screen capture, analytics or unintended recipients.
entries.remediation: Avoid copying active credentials when possible. For required clipboard operations, choose local-only sharing and an appropriate expiration, minimize copied data, and verify clearing behavior without disrupting unrelated clipboard content.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: The bad-certificate callback explicitly returns acceptance. Resolve the HttpClient or adapter instance and shipped build before concluding that failed certificate chains are accepted for sensitive requests.
entries.impact: A weak trust decision or sensitive cleartext request can expose credentials or let an intermediary alter application data.

entries.title: Sensitive Input Prediction Review
entries.description: The same TextField or TextFormField both obscures its input and enables autocorrection or suggestions. Verify whether sensitive values can reach keyboard prediction or learning services on each supported platform.
entries.impact: Sensitive information may reach logs, other applications, keyboard services, screen capture, analytics or unintended recipients.
entries.remediation: Disable autocorrection and suggestions for sensitive text fields, select appropriate secure input and autofill settings, and test actual keyboard behavior on Android and iOS.
entries.reviewer: Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

entries.title: WebView Navigation Policy Review
entries.description: A WebView origin whitelist contains a wildcard. Trace the content and native bridge privileges; static local HTML may legitimately require a wildcard, while external navigation needs instance-specific controls.
entries.impact: Untrusted frames or navigation may reach privileged native operations or expose session data if origin isolation and per-operation authorization are insufficient.
entries.remediation: Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.
entries.reviewer: Test subframes, redirects, javascript/data/content URLs, deceptive host suffixes, and a safe WebView beside an unsafe instance; JavaScript enablement alone is not a vulnerability.

entries.title: Native OAuth Proof-Key Protection Disabled
entries.description: An authorization-request configuration explicitly disables proof-key protection. Resolve the public native client and authorization-code flow; check the exact redirect handler and provider requirements.
entries.impact: A bypassed identity decision may grant access to protected actions or data, depending on server enforcement and key binding.
entries.remediation: Enforce authorization on the trusted server and bind local authentication to protected keys or credentials where required; use external-browser authorization and proof-key protection for public native clients.
entries.reviewer: Test cancellation, device-credential fallback, enrollment changes, stale reuse windows, redirect interception and unavailable secure storage; local biometrics do not replace server authorization.

entries.title: Secure Storage Backup Review
entries.description: The secure-store plugin's automatic Android backup configuration is disabled. Custom backup rules can make this legitimate; verify that encrypted entries are excluded from the actual cloud and transfer configurations.
entries.impact: Recoverable sensitive values may expose sessions or private data to a party able to access the relevant storage, backup or shared device.
entries.remediation: Keep privileged secrets on the server, use appropriate device-backed secure storage for local credentials, and restrict backup and sharing to intended non-sensitive data.
entries.reviewer: Test device lock state, cloud backup versus device transfer, restored keys, keychain persistence after reinstall, and secure-storage failure; do not silently fall back to plaintext or treat an unrelated secure store as protection.

entries.description: Hybrid server configuration allows wildcard navigation inside the privileged WebView. Resolve the generated configuration, release overrides and which plugin operations external content can invoke.

entries.title: WebView Navigation Policy Review
entries.description: The main hybrid WebView allows a broad class of navigation targets. Resolve CSP, redirects and plugin access; main-WebView rules do not automatically protect plugin or external-browser views.
entries.impact: Untrusted frames or navigation may reach privileged native operations or expose session data if origin isolation and per-operation authorization are insufficient.

entries.title: Remote Native Module Policy Review
entries.description: Configuration opts into remote modules for a native application. Resolve the release configuration, allowed URL prefixes and update integrity; downloaded modules may have native platform privileges.
entries.impact: Untrusted content may execute privileged behavior or overwrite files if integrity, type constraints or destination containment are ineffective.
entries.remediation: Verify signed updates and compatibility, restrict decoded types, and enforce canonical destination containment before extraction or execution.
entries.reviewer: Test tampered updates, downgrade/replay, absolute paths, traversal, sibling-prefix and symlink escapes, size limits and partial failure; an unrelated validation call does not protect this operation.

entries.title: Remote Native Module Loading Review
entries.description: An executable dynamic import names a remote HTTP or HTTPS module. Determine who controls that content and whether it is bundled, verified or replaceable after the application ships.
entries.impact: A caller outside the intended trust boundary may trigger privileged behavior or access data if component restrictions and runtime authorization are insufficient.
entries.remediation: Minimize exported surfaces and URI grants; validate parsed schemes, hosts and paths, use verified links where appropriate, and authorize each sensitive action.
entries.reviewer: Resolve merged manifests, aliases and SDK defaults; test custom-scheme collision, malformed URLs, encoded paths, nested intents, read/write grants and permission inheritance. Registration or permission presence alone does not prove unauthorized access.

entries.title: Security-Sensitive Randomness Review
entries.description: General-purpose Random generates a value assigned to a security-named variable. Verify whether the value is a token, key, nonce or other security material; non-security randomized behavior is outside this check.
entries.impact: Weak or predictable protection can expose sensitive values or allow unauthorized modification when used at a security boundary.
entries.remediation: Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.
entries.reviewer: Distinguish checksums from authentication, asymmetric RSA transformations from symmetric ECB, and test IV/nonce reuse, fixed keys and algorithm migration.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: An executable certificate-failure callback explicitly returns acceptance without testing the certificate. Resolve the HTTP client instance and selected build.
entries.impact: If this callback is used for sensitive requests, a failed certificate chain may be accepted and allow interception or response tampering. Actual hostname handling and adapter versions require review.
entries.remediation: Use the platform certificate trust checks and remove unconditional acceptance callbacks from shipped clients. If private trust is necessary, validate the intended chain and hostname for this exact connection.
entries.reviewer: Test invalid certificates and wrong hosts for the affected client; an unrelated pinned client does not protect it. Conditional callbacks and static examples must not be reported as unconditional acceptance.

entries.title: Release Debug Signing Review
entries.description: The release build directly references the debug signing configuration. Resolve CI overrides and verify the certificate in the distributed artifact.
entries.impact: A distributed application signed with a known or development key can lose release identity assurance and may be unsuitable for trusted distribution.
entries.remediation: Use the authorized release signing identity or app-signing workflow, protect signing access and verify the resulting certificate.
entries.reviewer: Verify the selected build and active callers. Retain unresolved evidence when runtime, backend or generated configuration is unavailable.

entries.title: Provider Stream Read Review
entries.negative: try (InputStream input = resolver.openInputStream(uri)) { while ((count = input.read(buffer)) != -1) { writeBounded(buffer, count); } }
entries.description: A provider stream is sized with available() and read once without checking the returned byte count. This is not a reliable complete or bounded file read.
entries.impact: Partial reads can corrupt uploaded content; large provider-reported sizes can cause excessive allocation. Exploitability depends on the selected provider and active caller.
entries.remediation: Use bounded streaming, handle null and partial reads, enforce limits while consuming input and close streams on all paths.
entries.reviewer: Verify the selected build and active callers. Retain unresolved evidence when runtime, backend or generated configuration is unavailable.

entries.title: Privacy API Purpose Description Review
entries.description: A supported protected-resource API in the supplied source has no resolved nonempty purpose description in this application plist. Resolve active callers, generated settings, localization and API-specific platform requirements.
entries.impact: A missing effective purpose description can prevent a protected operation or fail platform privacy requirements; API presence alone does not establish data disclosure.
entries.remediation: Supply a meaningful description for the used resource in the selected target and localization, request only required access and test denied/restricted behavior.
entries.reviewer: Verify the selected build and active callers. Retain unresolved evidence when runtime, backend or generated configuration is unavailable.

entries.title: Credential Backup Policy Review
entries.description: A credential-related preferences write is correlated with a source backup policy that may include that store. Resolve OS and target SDK behavior, build resources and actual value protection.
entries.impact: Permitted backup or device-transfer contents may retain reusable credentials if storage protection and policy do not exclude them. This does not imply public backup access.
entries.remediation: Avoid password retention, use appropriate platform-backed credential protection and exclude credential stores from relevant backup and transfer scopes.
entries.reviewer: Verify the selected build and active callers. Retain unresolved evidence when runtime, backend or generated configuration is unavailable.

entries.title: OTP Completion Without Verification Review
entries.description: The OTP completion callback advances navigation without a preceding verification operation in the recorded callback. Filling a field does not establish proof of possession.
entries.impact: The client may advance an account verification flow on arbitrary entered digits. Backend verification and the shipped route must be reviewed before claiming account takeover.
entries.remediation: Require a successful verification result before advancing; bind the verified account and challenge on the backend. Resolve delegated verification and failure paths explicitly.

entries.title: Persisted Account State Retained During Local Logout Review
entries.description: An imported logout action clears a token while the locally bound reducer spread preserves account-related fields in an AsyncStorage-persisted root reducer.
entries.impact: Account-related data may remain on the device or be reused across account changes if no other cleanup occurs. This does not establish server-session reuse or actual cross-account disclosure.
entries.remediation: Reset account-scoped memory and persisted state on logout/account change, await persistent cleanup, and verify backend session revocation. Check delegated cleanup and persistence transforms.

entries.title: Credential Parameter in HTTP Request Review
entries.positive: import com.android.volley.toolbox.StringRequest; import com.android.volley.toolbox.Volley; StringRequest request=new StringRequest(POST,"http://service.invalid/login",ok,fail){ protected Map<String,String> getParams(){ Map<String,String> params=new HashMap<>(); params.put("password",password); return params; }}; Volley.newRequestQueue(this).add(request);
entries.negative: import com.android.volley.toolbox.StringRequest; import com.android.volley.toolbox.Volley; StringRequest request=new StringRequest(POST,"https://service.invalid/login",ok,fail){ protected Map<String,String> getParams(){ Map<String,String> params=new HashMap<>(); params.put("password",password); return params; }}; Volley.newRequestQueue(this).add(request);
entries.description: An enqueued Volley StringRequest returns a credential-named parameter and its locally resolved endpoint uses HTTP. This links the request body and URL rather than unrelated file keywords.
entries.impact: Reusable plaintext credentials can be observed or modified in transit when this request executes and cleartext is permitted. Value protection, selected transport policy, release inclusion and server behavior require confirmation.
entries.remediation: Use authenticated HTTPS for credential-bearing requests, remove cleartext exceptions for sensitive endpoints, and avoid transmitting reusable passwords beyond the required login exchange.
entries.reviewer: Resolve the same returned parameter, endpoint, queue submission and selected network policy. An unresolved URL or unsupported request abstraction is a coverage limit, not proof of secure transport.
